headline: High-risk write/egress asymmetry: AutoGen can execute code and write files while MinerU ingests documents via MCP/API, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell code, while MinerU exposes document inputs and an MCP server. If MinerU outputs are routed into AutoGen without sanitization, document content can steer tool use. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are copied into AutoGen prompts or files without filtering
IF AutoGen is configured to treat document text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt wrapper that labels MinerU text as untrusted
Strip tool directives from extracted documents before passing them onward
Use separate workspaces for extraction and agent execution
Review one sample document flow end-to-end before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and broad filesystem access; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text through API/MCP surfaces. If both share a workspace or the same files, sensitive document contents can flow into AutoGen outputs or external model calls. The docs do not prove a shared directory, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted workspace
IF AutoGen forwards document text to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Place MinerU inputs and AutoGen outputs in separate directories
Disable AutoGen access to sensitive folders
Use redacted sample documents for integration testing
Confirm model-provider logging settings before processing real data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; MinerU supports concurrent inference and MCP/API access. Even without explicit git writes, overlapping mutable access to shared files can race or overwrite outputs. Because shared-state details are developer-defined, the conflict is plausible but not fully documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same output directory
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking
mitigations: Assign each agent its own output directory
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs during integration tests
Check for clobbered files after one trial run

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing system that can emit OCR text and structured extractions; AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestrator that can act on tool outputs. If AutoGen consumes MinerU extractions as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pairwise interaction is documented only indirectly, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF AutoGen uses MinerU output as a source of facts without verification
IF downstream agents or tools act on those facts
mitigations: Require a human review step for extracted facts
Keep original documents linked beside extracted text
Add confidence thresholds before acting on OCR results
Run one validation pass comparing extraction to source pages

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is that AutoGen can handle model-provider API keys while MinerU processes document files; without a documented mismatch, only a low residual gap is visible. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through a non-approved model provider via AutoGen
IF MinerU inputs include data subject to stricter retention rules than the downstream model
mitigations: Verify data-class handling rules before production use
Route regulated documents only through approved providers
Document retention settings for both systems
Test deletion/export handling on one sample record
